paper_title: VisuoThink Empowering LVLM Reasoning with Multimodal Tree Search
caption: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (right) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with both GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of child nodes in a tree width and the accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) for GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet. The x-axis represents the number of child nodes, ranging from 1 to 7, with tick labels spaced every 1 unit. The y-axis represents accuracy@1, measured as a percentage, displayed on a linear scale ranging from 15% to 35%, with tick intervals of 5%. A solid purple line represents GPT-4o, beginning at approximately 28.9% at 3 child nodes, rising to a peak of around 34.4% at 5 child nodes, and then declining to approximately 31.1% at 7 child nodes. A dashed blue line represents Claude-3.5-Sonnet, starting at approximately 26.7% at 3 child nodes, increasing to around 28% at 5 child nodes, and subsequently decreasing to approximately 20% at 7 child nodes.
